text:
alex: heads up — i opened a small runtime PR that touches the batching scheduling and a KV cache TTL edgecase. hoping to merge in the 1h maintenance window if no objections. link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/892

maria: on it, grabbing a quick look now. can you paste the perf numbers you saw locally?

alex: sure — local perf: tail latency p95 dropped ~8% for short sequences with the new batch-split heuristic. no throughput regressions on our 16xA100 sim.

sam: fyi i'm oncall until 15:30, can review after that if you still need. if it's urgent, @maria should be able to give quick eyes.

dena: quick question — the KV TTL change bumps the default from 60s -> 90s, was that to address the cold-prefix spike? will that affect memory churn for long-lived streams?

alex: exactly, the 90s fixes a rare prefetch-miss cascade we saw on convo-heavy workloads. memory bump looks <2% on our traces but i can add a config flag to keep old default for Dedicated tenants.

maria: skimmed diff — looks clean. small nit on comment for BatchSplitter: please clarify why we limit split by token_len not token_count.

alex: good catch — will update the comment in a follow-up commit.

ci-bot: CI passed — unit tests (45/45) ✅  integration smoke checks OK.

dena: I ran the small repro from the ticket against this branch, behavior fixed. no leaks observed after 10k steps.

sam: reread, left one inline comment about backoff math. overall lgtm from me if that is clarified.

maria: i can approve once the comment and the config feature flag are added. can you push the tiny edits?

alex: pushing a small commit now with the comment + feature flag toggle.

ci-bot: new build queued for commit a7f3c2d — tests running.

maria: approved :white_check_mark:  — merge when green and you have the slot.

alex: sweet — i'll merge in 30m if CI stays clean, thanks everyone.
